title: Sprint deck: seed & scale ops cribsheet (draft)
content:
Purpose: single-sheet speaker-backed deck to help SEs run a pilot from seed->scale in 10 steps. Draft and intentionally scrappy: checklist + quick rebuttals + minimal diagrams for 3-minute technical sell. Keep this as a living cribsheet; use during pre-call prep and in-runway huddles.

Audience: Sales Engineers, Solutions Engineers, Platform / Integration Engineers who run pilots, early adoption POC owners. Not a legal doc — use as tactical field reference.

Slide 1 — Headline + TL;DR
- Headline: 'Pilot Roadmap: Seed -> Scale in 30 days (ops-first)'.
- TL;DR bullets for buyer: predictable latency, fallback plan, measurable unit economics.
- Quick field note (speaker): Lead with guardrail: "We'll validate performance and cost on your real traffic; we'll ship a safe fallback if anything surprises us."

Slide 2 — One-line value props (engineer-focused)
- Predictable throughput: reserved capacity/auto-burst options.
- Cost controls: batching, KV-cache, quantization recommendations.
- Reliability: multi-tier fallback, canary rollouts, routing policy.
- Speaker note: call out how these map to SLOs they care about (p95 latency, 99.9% availability for inference endpoint).

Slide 3 — 10-step pilot checklist (runbook) 
- 0. Pre-qual: confirm business metric and max acceptable p95 latency.
- 1. Baseline: snapshot current API call volumes, median/95th lat, token distribution. (ask for 72h logs)
- 2. Data access: confirm ephemeral sample payloads & privacy constraints.
- 3. Model choice & config: pick model family + quantization target; note tradeoffs.
- 4. Capacity plan: reserved vs. burst; set initial concurrency.
- 5. Instrumentation: attach tracing token, sample requests, and logging level.
- 6. Canary: route 1–5% traffic for 24h, monitor lat & error increase.
- 7. Fallbacks: define model variant and regional fallback. Include rate limiting guardrail.
- 8. Quality evals: run prompt set (20 golden prompts) and collect failure modes.
- 9. Cost validation: run continuous cost sim for production mix (24–72h).
- 10. Scale: ramp by factors (5x) with throttled windows, confirm autoscaling behavior.

Slide 4 — Short decision matrix (customer tier + suggested approach)
- Startup/PoC: hosted API, default small-reserved pool, aggressive caching.
- Platform: dedicated reserved capacity + canary policies + SSO & audit logs.
- Regulated: private deployment (VPC) with KMS & longer lead time for capacity.
- Speaker note: map to procurement triggers and typical procurement blockers.

Slide 5 — Objection quick hits (top 6)
- 'Costs will spike' — reply: show quick econ: token-level cost + batching delta; propose 2-week cost cap.
- 'Latency unpredictable' — reply: present p95 guarantees + canary routing + regional fallback.
- 'Data residency/compliance' — reply: private deployment path, audit logs, KMS.
- 'Model quality regressions' — reply: rollout with eval suite + rollback hook.
- 'We need on-prem' — reply: private pack + airgap checklist (timeline 6–8 weeks).
- 'What happens if the model mis-behaves in production?' — reply: circuit-breaker + human-in-loop flags + rollback policy.

Slide 6 — Quick fallback playbook (ops steps)
- Trigger conditions: p95 > baseline * 1.5 for 15m OR error-rate > 1% for 5m.
- First action (automated): shift 30% traffic to cached responses / smaller-model variant.
- Second action (SE-run): increase model variant concurrency, enable low-latency quantized path.
- Third action: region failover to cold standby, notify customer via configured webhook.
- Post-mortem: record incident tags, attach trace IDs, follow 48h follow-up call.

Slide 7 — Quality gating checklist (for SE-run rollouts)
- Golden prompts pass rate >= 95%
- Embedding similarity distribution within expected band
- No category of semantic regression observed (NLP eval notes)
- Latency / cost within agreed SLOs

Slide 8 — Sample pilot metrics dashboard (what to share)
- KPI: p95 latency, p50 latency, QPS, tokens per request, cost per 1k responses, golden prompts pass rate.
- Operational alerts: sustained error-rate > 0.5%, p95 spike > 50% baseline, cache-hit-rate < 40%.

Slide 9 — Play-by-play speaker bullets for a 10-min tech demo
- 0–30s: Quick intro & outcome (reduce latency, keep cost predictable).
- 30–90s: Architecture sketch (client -> Redwood API -> model pool -> fallback).
- 90–180s: Live demo with sample prompt + show latency & token meter.
- 180–300s: Show canary routing toggle, fallback demo, and audit traces.
- 300–600s: Next steps & ask (access to 72h logs, golden prompt set, exec sponsor).

Slide 10 — Field-play attachments (appendix)
- Quick email template to request logs from customer (paste-ready).
- Minimal infra diagram (ASCII) and curl example for canary.
- Runbook snippet for urgent rollback.

Appendix: paste-ready artifacts
- Email request (sample):
  Subject: Pilot data & quick ask — [COMPANY] Redwood pilot
  Body: Hi [name],
  We need a 72-hour sample of inference logs (anonymized is fine) to baseline latency and token distribution. Also please share 10–20 golden prompts used in production. We’ll use these only for evaluation and will purge after the pilot.
  Thanks,
  Maya (SE)

- cURL canary toggle example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/canary -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route": "canary-1", "fraction": 0.02}'

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Confirm sample payload anonymization constraints with legal for regulated verticals.
- Add one-pager for Finance to pre-approve cost cap contract template.
- Validate "airgap timeline" with private-deploy engineering (is 6–8 weeks accurate?).

Usage guidance for SEs (checklist to print as one-pager)
- Pre-call: load this cribsheet, attach relevant logs link, set up recording.
- During call: use the objection hits, ask for golden prompts early, propose quick cost cap.
- Post-call: create JIRA ticket using template JIRA-PILOT-XXXX and tag eng-sre.

Speaker closing note: keep it focused on predictable outcomes and a short path to a safe rollback. This doc helps you move quickly while keeping guardrails in place.

Revision history (tiny)
- 2025-11-03: initial draft by Maya Chen
- 2026-01-10: added fallback automation snippets (Samir)
- 2026-02-20: tightened metrics & added cost crawl guidance (Priya)

End of cribsheet.
